messages:
Sanjay: RFC follow-up on Triton vs CUTLASS attention kernels. Quick summary: Triton = fast iteration (Python/JIT), CUTLASS = hand-tuned throughput on long seqs / quantized paths, but higher infra + maintenance cost. Need choice or hybrid strategy + concrete action items. RFC: https://rfc.internal/triton-cutlass-attn

Lia: +1 on hybrid thinking. Triton dev velocity is huge but we've hit ABI churn before. Need a stable adapter surface.

Mike: Posted a short perf summary: Triton ~95% of CUTLASS on seq <=1024, drops to ~80% on 4k+; CUTLASS wins int8 quantized end-to-end. Link: https://perf/reports/1789 (charts)

ci-bot: Benchmark run finished: https://ci.internal/builds/attn-bench-1789. Includes fq/latency/throughput. (auto)

Elaine: Operational flag: CUTLASS adds large compile time and increases container sizes. For Hosted we should avoid full CUTLASS in default images. Dedicated/Private could opt-in.

TJ: Suggestion: kernel adapter + runtime routing. Default: Triton kernels. Fallback: CUTLASS for heavy sequences or when int8 path required. Need a small ABI and a runtime decision policy.

Sanjay: Proposed minimal KernelInterface v0 (sketch):
```
int kernel_init(const char* cfg_json);
int kernel_supports(const char* op, const char* tag);
int kernel_attention_forward(void* ctx, const float* qkv, float* out, const void* params);
int kernel_shutdown();
// returns standardized memory layout tags: "KV_v2", "packed_qkv"
```
Keep the interface C-compatible; expose a thin Python wrapper for Triton adapters.

Lia: C ABI is reasonable. Concern: Triton wrappers will still require Python runtime for JIT. We should ensure adapter can be loaded from runtime without reloading python sub-interpreter for every worker. Also add a canary job in CI that runs each adapter.

Mike: I'll start a PoC Triton adapter reusing runtime/triton/kernels/attention/*. Will add perf counters and a tiny compatibility shim to satisfy the C API. Need a builder node for CUTLASS experiments.

Elaine: I'll provision a CUTLASS build VM (CUDA 12 + cuBLAS + CUTLASS pinned hash) and try a "cutlass-lite" subset: only attention-related kernels + int8 GEMMs to reduce build time.

TJ: Important: KV caching layout must be identical. Any adapter must accept KV layout v2.0 (see runtime/kv/layout_v2.md). I'll add regression tests that replay recorded traces.

Sanjay: Action items (owners + rough due dates):
- A1: KernelInterface spec + API doc (owner: Lia) - due in 5 business days.
- A2: Triton adapter PoC + perf harness integration (owner: Mike) - initial results in 10 business days.
- A3: CUTLASS-lite build experiment + image size analysis (owner: Elaine) - 10 business days.
- A4: Bench harness extension for quantized attention tests (owner: TJ) - 7 business days.

ci-bot: Created tickets: https://jira.internal/browse/KER-3421 KInterface spec, KER-3422 Triton PoC, KER-3423 CUTLASS build, KER-3424 bench ext (auto)

Lia: One more ask: add a feature flag gating fallback to CUTLASS per-customer (for Dedicated/Private). We should avoid exposing it to Hosted until we have measurable stability.

Elaine: Note: CUTLASS provides int8 GEMM now; Triton would need custom int8 kernels. That will affect timelines for quantized path.

Sanjay: Decision for now: proceed with hybrid approach + interface. Implement PoC and run 2-week benchmark cycle. If CUTLASS shows >10% consistent uplift on our target workloads, we promote it to stable fallback with rollout plan. Otherwise keep Triton as primary but keep adapter available.

Mike: Acknowledged. I'll open a draft PR for the PoC tomorrow and link the perf rig.

Elaine: I'll share CUTLASS-lite build logs in #eng-infra when ready.

TJ: I'll add KV-layout tests to the bench harness and wire them to the new tickets.

Sanjay: Thanks all. Will follow up in 2 weeks with consolidated results. :thumbsup:

Lia: :thumbsup:

Mike: :rocket:
